Step: Declare SEV1; open #inc-<date>-prod-rds, bridge; assign IC, Executor, 2nd eyes, DBA, Comms, Scribe; pin this runbook. dr_mark T1
[Investigating] comms: chat now; leadership + status page ≤ 30 min (templates)
Set T0 from the first failing synthetic / 5xx: dr_mark T0 --at <ts> source=<monitor>
Confirm the scenario: RDS events + status of $PRIMARY_DB; no Multi-AZ failover in progress or it failed; data is correct (not a corruption incident)

Pre-flight: dr_run preflight ./automation/scripts/dr-preflight.sh replica (replica available + replicating/error, ReplicaLag vs RPO, LSN/heartbeat SQL, creds work on the replica, EKS + ESO + Reloader healthy, consumer inventory)
Expected / verify: PRE-FLIGHT: PASS, or a waiver per FAIL

Step: Declare DR (IC + Service Owner; + exec if est. loss > RPO). GO if the primary is not recoverable within (RTO − measured promote+cutover time)
Expected / verify: DECISION: G1 GO est_loss=<s> · dr_mark T2

Step: Fence OLD_DB (CP-04) level F2 quarantine SG if the API accepts it; otherwise record a waiver: dr_mark FENCE "level=none waiver=<reason>"

Snapshot the old instance before any destructive action, if it is reachable: aws rds create-db-snapshot --db-instance-identifier $OLD_DB --db-snapshot-identifier ${OLD_DB}-pre-fence-$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M) (can run ‖ with the fence)
Apply the fence level chosen in the table above; the script saves the before-state (SG IDs, parameter values) into evidence
Verify: ./automation/scripts/dr-verify.sh connections shows 0 app sessions on OLD_DB (F1/F2)
Record the fence state and any waiver in the timeline: dr_mark FENCE "level=F2 waiver=none"
CP01-S01…S03: consumer inventory, suspend rotation, suspend CronJobs
Capture the final replica state (RPO evidence): dr_run replica-final psql "$TARGET_DSN" -XAt -f automation/sql/10-preflight-replica.sql
Expected / verify: LSN + last replay ts + heartbeat saved

Step: Point of no return (IC + DBA): fence status accepted, final LSN captured. Approve in SSM (aws:approve)
[Failover Initiated] comms, all audiences
Promote (manual fallback): dr_mark T4 · aws rds promote-read-replica --db-instance-identifier $REPLICA_DB --backup-retention-period 14

Wait until standalone: ./automation/scripts/dr-verify.sh wait-promoted. ⚠ Do not trust wait db-instance-available alone: the instance can still show available *before* the promotion starts. The script waits for: no ReadReplicaSourceDBInstanceIdentifier + available + pg_is_in_recovery()=f. dr_mark T5

CP-01 S04 → S09: pre-verify creds on TARGET_DB → cutover gate (= G3) → update $SECRET_ID host → force ESO sync → Reloader rollouts → RO secret ($SECRET_ID_RO → TARGET_DB, because there is no replica now) → unannotated consumers. Marks T6, T7
Inventory consumers: ./automation/scripts/dr-eks-rollout.sh inventory lists every workload that mounts/env-refs $K8S_SECRET, with or without a Reloader annotation
Expected / verify: No unannotated consumers, or the list is noted for manual restart

Step: Suspend secret rotation (a rotation run would race with the cutover): aws secretsmanager cancel-rotate-secret --secret-id $SECRET_ID (only if RotationEnabled=true; record this so rotation is re-enabled in CP-03)
Suspend CronJobs that use the DB: ./automation/scripts/dr-eks-rollout.sh suspend-cronjobs

Pre-verify credentials on TARGET_DB *before* switching: ./automation/scripts/dr-secret-cutover.sh precheck. ⚠ S3/S4 trap: a restored DB holds passwords as of the restore point. If the app password was rotated since then, the current secret password fails. The script reports this, and fix-password resets the role password on TARGET_DB to the current secret value (needs the master credentials)
Expected / verify: login OK as $APP_DB_USER on TARGET_DB, pg_is_in_recovery=f

Step: Cutover gate (PROD: G3 of the parent runbook): TARGET_DB verified, the old instance is fenced or agreed not to be, and comms are ready. DECISION: CUTOVER GO

Update the secret: ./automation/scripts/dr-secret-cutover.sh apply. It saves the previous VersionId and host (never the password) into evidence, sets host, port, dbInstanceIdentifier (if present), calls put-secret-value, then dr_mark T6
Expected / verify: New VersionId is AWSCURRENT; old is AWSPREVIOUS

Step: Force ESO sync (do not wait up to refreshInterval): run by the script: kubectl annotate externalsecret $K8S_SECRET force-sync=$(date +%s) --overwrite
Expected / verify: ExternalSecret Ready=True, refreshTime after T6; K8s Secret DB_HOST = new endpoint

Step: Wait for the Reloader rollouts: ./automation/scripts/dr-eks-rollout.sh wait (waits on rollout status for every annotated consumer, in restart-order). Fallback if Reloader is down or not annotated: ./automation/scripts/dr-eks-rollout.sh restart. Then dr_mark T7
Expected / verify: All successfully rolled out; 0 pods older than T6 among consumers

Step: Read-only secret (UAT/PROD, if SECRET_ID_RO is used by read paths that pointed at the replica, which is gone, stale or now primary): SECRET_ID=$SECRET_ID_RO ./automation/scripts/dr-secret-cutover.sh apply (temporarily points reads at TARGET_DB). Restore a proper replica in the FB runbook
Expected / verify: Reader pods rolled; no connections to the old replica

Step: Restart unannotated consumers from S01, delete/re-run in-flight Jobs, and resume CronJobs *after* CP-02 passes: ./automation/scripts/dr-eks-rollout.sh resume-cronjobs
If OLD_DB was not fenced: check it for app sessions now (dr-verify.sh connections) and fence as soon as it becomes reachable
CP-02 (S01, S03–S07). dr_mark T9, G4 → T10. [Services Restored] comms

DB checks on the current primary: dr_run db-post psql "$TARGET_DSN" -f automation/sql/20-postfailover-verify.sql (not in recovery, not read-only, write probe, invalid indexes, leftover slots, connection headroom)

Restore-point validation (S3/S4 only): psql "$TARGET_DSN" -v cutoff="'<restore time>'" -f automation/sql/05-restore-point-check.sql. The latest business timestamps must match the expected restore point, and the bad data (for a data incident) must be absent
Expected / verify: App owner signs off: "data as of <ts>, bad change absent"

Step: App connections land on TARGET_DB: ./automation/scripts/dr-verify.sh connections (counts pg_stat_activity by application_name on TARGET and OLD instances)
Expected / verify: TARGET has the expected consumers; OLD has 0 app sessions

Step: App deep health: ./automation/scripts/dr-verify.sh app (readiness/deep-health endpoints of critical services)
Synthetic business transactions (login → read → create/save → background job processed)
Expected / verify: All pass. The first of 3 consecutive greens = dr_mark T9

Step: Error/latency SLO for 15 min (5xx rate, p95, DB errors such as could not connect / read-only transaction)
Async paths: queues draining, CronJobs resumed (CP01-S09), integrations (in/outbound) processing

Performance after restore (S3/S4): restored volumes lazy-load from S3, so the first reads are slow. Warm the hot tables: psql "$TARGET_DSN" -f automation/sql/06-warmup.sql (pg_prewarm) and watch ReadLatency/DiskQueueDepth
Declare service restored (IC) → dr_mark T10 → send [Services Restored] comms
CP-03 parity + Multi-AZ conversion (CP03-S03) the same day + alarm re-pointing + baseline snapshot

Parity diff: ./automation/scripts/rds-config-parity.sh $OLD_DB $TARGET_DB (compares class, storage, Multi-AZ, SGs, PG, backup retention/window, maintenance window, PI, monitoring, log exports, IAM auth, CA, deletion protection, tags)
Expected / verify: The diff list is the to-do list

Step: Apply the missing settings: aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier $TARGET_DB --apply-immediately --backup-retention-period <n> --deletion-protection --enable-performance-insights --monitoring-interval 60 --monitoring-role-arn <arn> --cloudwatch-logs-export-configuration '{"EnableLogTypes":["postgresql","upgrade"]}' ... and aws rds add-tags-to-resource ...
Expected / verify: Re-run parity: no diffs (except accepted ones)

Step: PROD only: Multi-AZ aws rds modify-db-instance --db-instance-identifier $TARGET_DB --multi-az --apply-immediately (online, but adds I/O load while the standby is built; prefer a quiet period the same day)

Monitoring re-point: alarms (DBInstanceIdentifier dimension), dashboards, RDS event subscription source IDs, Datadog/Prometheus config → TARGET_DB. Run ./automation/scripts/rds-config-parity.sh --alarms $OLD_DB $TARGET_DB
Expected / verify: Alarms for TARGET_DB exist and are OK (not INSUFFICIENT_DATA)

Step: Re-enable rotation (if it was enabled): aws secretsmanager rotate-secret --secret-id $SECRET_ID --rotation-rules AutomaticallyAfterDays=30 (the rotation Lambda reads host from the secret, so it now targets TARGET_DB). Do it after T10 + 2 h

Backups: confirm the AWS Backup plan selects TARGET_DB (tag), take a manual baseline snapshot aws rds create-db-snapshot --db-instance-identifier $TARGET_DB --db-snapshot-identifier ${TARGET_DB}-baseline-$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M)
IaC adoption (§3)
⚠ Residual risk: PROD has no read replica until RB-PROD-FB-S2. Do FB-S2 phase 1 (create the replica) within 24 h
CP-05 evidence + KPIs; CP-06 PIR

Record the RPO inputs on the timeline (see docs/04): S1 → dr_mark RPO_ZERO (synchronous standby); S2 → RPO_LAST_REPLICATED (heartbeat on the promoted DB) + RPO_LAST_PRIMARY_COMMIT; S3 → dr_mark RPO_SNAPSHOT "value=<SnapshotCreateTime>"; S4 → dr_mark RPO_RESTORE_TS "value=<restore-time>" (plus DAMAGE_STOPPED / FENCE markers, which bound the loss window)

Collect evidence + KPIs: ./automation/scripts/dr-collect-evidence.sh (CloudTrail, RDS events, describe before/after, secret version stages (no values), k8s rollouts, SQL outputs, timeline, manifest + SHA-256 → S3 Object Lock)
Expected / verify: EVIDENCE: s3://… sha256=… posted in the channel

Step: Post the KPI table (rto-rpo-report.md) in the incident channel and the ticket
Raise the FB / normalisation change for the scenario (see the catalogue) with an owner and date
Schedule the post-incident review (CP-06): PROD ≤ 5 business days; UAT ≤ 10; DEV optional
